ZiChuanLan/agent-purge.content:
# agent-purge

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/agent-purge)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-purge)
[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/ZiChuanLan/agent-purge)](https://github.com/ZiChuanLan/agent-purge/stargazers)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/agent-purge)](LICENSE)

一份系统提示词，喂给多个 coding agent。支持替换（replace）、只发人设（strict）、追加（append）、清空（off）四种模式，可热切换，全程可逆。

```
agent-purge web          # 本地控制台 http://127.0.0.1:7788
agent-purge codex        # 用当前 persona 启动 codex
agent-purge pi --ask "…" # 一次性提问
```

## 它做什么

每家 coding agent 读系统提示词的位置都不一样：有的认启动参数，有的认配置文件，有的只能靠插件改运行时对象。agent-purge 把这些入口统一成三件事：

| 通道 | 机制 | 生效范围 |
|---|---|---|
| `install` | 写入该 harness 的托管配置块（Markdown / hooks / 插件） | 常驻，别人启动也生效 |
| `shim` | 往 PATH 前置同名小壳，转发给 `agent-purge <h>` | 裸敲命令也接管 |
| `slash` | 会话内 `/purge on\|off\|status` | 热切换，不动磁盘 |

三层都写的是同一份 `personas/<id>.md` 的正文。`--mode off` 或 Web 总开关关掉时，全部撤回到原样——不留残渣。

## 安装

```bash
npm i -g agent-purge     # 或 npx agent-purge web
```

要求 Node ≥ 20，零依赖。

**数据独立存放**，升级不会被覆盖：默认 `~/.agent-purge/`（Windows `C:\Users\<你>\.agent-purge\`），里面是 `state.json` 和 `personas/`。想换位置就设环境变量：

```bash
export AGENT_PURGE_HOME=/path/to/your/data     # Windows: setx AGENT_PURGE_HOME D:\ap-data
```

旧版本（0.1.x）把数据放在包目录里，首次运行会自动搬到新家，原文件不动。

## 人设

`personas/<id>.md` = frontmatter + 正文。正文就是会被写进系统提示词的那一段。

frontmatter 用 `description` 写「说明」（Web 列表和 `agent-purge ls` 显示的就是它）；旧的 `desc` 仍然认，不会报错。可选 `order`（排序）、`harness` / `model`（匹配用）。Web 里只改名字和说明时会保留 frontmatter 的其它键，不整段重写。

```bash
agent-purge ls                 # 列出全部 persona，标出当前匹配的
agent-purge use <id>           # 切换当前 persona
agent-purge pi --persona <id>  # 只这一轮用别的
```

首次运行会在 `personas/` 下生成 `neutral.md` 起步模板。

## 支持情况

每个数字都是实测值：本地假 provider 抓真实请求体，不是估算。

| harness | 机制 | 实测版本 | 默认 system | 注入后 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `codex` | 启动参数 `-c model_instructions_file=` | 0.163.0 | 21,026 | 24 |
| `claude` | `--system-prompt-file` + 二进制补丁清残留身份句 | 2.1.304 | 6,379 | 156 |
| `grok` | `--system-prompt-override` | 1.0.62 | 5,146 | 21 |
| `omp` | `--system-prompt` | 17.4.2 | 34,511 | 10,106 |
| `hermes` | 临时 HOME 里替换 `SOUL.md` | 0.21.5 | 8,139 | 7,554 |
| `zcode` | UserPromptSubmit hook（user 角色）+ `customSystemPrompt` | 0.16.9 | 9,359 | 9,359 |
| `opencode` | cwd 下 `.opencode/plugin/*.ts` 原地改 `output.system` | 1.19.3 | 19,332 | 112 |
| `opencode2` | `plugins/agent-purge-v2.ts` 的 `ctx.session.hook("context")` | 0.0.0-beta-17823 | 8,279 | 3,189 |
| `dsh` | cordis 插件（三个 profile 各一份） | 0.2.1-rc.2 | 5,713 | 68 |
| `pi` | 原生扩展，会话内 `/purge` | — | — | — |
| `antigravity` | 等长替换二进制里的身份句 | 1.23.x | ≈20,498 | — |
| `codebuddy` | `--system-prompt-file` | 2.171.0 | — | — |
| `qoder` / `workbuddy` | 不支持（提示词在服务端） | — | — | — |

`opencode` 和 `opencode2` 是两个不同的 npm 包（`opencode-ai` 1.x 与 `@opencode/cli` 2.x），插件接口完全不同，各自独立支持。

`agent-purge ls` 和 Web 控制台显示的是**运行期真值**：每个 harness 有没有装、版本、注入层（SYS / USER）、三个通道各自可用性。`matrix.json` 里是静态能力表，两者冲突时以运行期为准。

闭源桌面端（提示词在服务端或二进制里）只做原样启动，不做任何注入——`agent-purge <h>` 会明确打印原因，不会假装生效。

# Kargul Calender Design Prototype

A design prototype of **Kargul Workspace**, a people-ops workspace built from the
"Dashboard – calendar" Figma design. Live at https://calender-app-design.vercel.app.

The **Time off** page (`/time-off`, the default route) reproduces the design
pixel-for-pixel; every other page in the sidebar is built in the same visual
language. Everything runs in the browser — there is no backend; data persists
to `localStorage`.

## Stack

- **Next.js 16** (App Router, Turbopack) · **React 19** · **TypeScript**
- **Tailwind CSS v4** with design tokens mapped from the Figma variables
- **shadcn/ui** (Radix primitives) themed to the design
- **Zustand** for state (`persist` middleware → `localStorage`)
- **next-themes** for dark mode, **Sonner** for toasts, **cmdk** for the command palette

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:3000. To return to the exact design state, use
**Settings → Data → Reset demo data** (or clear site data).

## What works

- **Calendar** — week / day / month views; drag on empty space to create, drag
  events to move (across days), drag the bottom edge to resize; overlapping
  events lay out side by side; all-day lane with public holidays; live now-line;
  origin-aware details popover.
- **Time off** — request dialog that counts working days (skips weekends and
  holidays) and shows the balance after the request; stats computed from your
  requests and allowance; requests table with search, filters, sorting, details,
  edit/cancel/delete, and a manager approve/decline preview.
- **Shell** — workspace switcher, ⌘K search across pages/events/requests/
  documents/invoices, notifications, help menu, dark mode, account menu.
- **Keyboard** — `⌘K` search, `N` new event, `R` request time-off, `T` today,
  `←/→` previous/next, `D/W/M` views, `?` shortcuts.
- **Other pages** — Dashboard, Analytics, Personal details, Documents, Time
  tracking, Benefits, Invoice, Withdrawal methods, Settings.

## Project layout

```
src/
  app/                 routes (one folder per sidebar page)
  components/
    ui/                shadcn/ui primitives, themed
    shell/             title bar, sidebar, search, notifications, shortcuts
    calendar/          header, time grid, all-day row, month view, popover
    time-off/          stats panel, requests table, status badge
    dialogs/           app-wide dialogs (request, event, details, holidays…)
    pages/             page bodies for the secondary routes
  stores/              Zustand stores (app data, calendar view, overlays)
  hooks/               client-only "today"/"now"
  lib/                 types, date helpers, leave rules, seed data
```

The seed in `src/lib/seed.ts` is what the design shows: the week of Nov 8–14,
2026 with Tue Nov 10 selected, and allowance figures of 7 available, 2 pending,
3 upcoming.

# MotionSites Web Builder: a free Claude skill

**Make Claude build award-level, cinematic landing pages instead of average AI layouts.**

AI-built websites tend to look the same for three reasons: a vague plan, no real media, and nobody looking at the result. This skill fixes all three. Claude studies the most-liked designs from [MotionSites](https://motionsites.ai/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=claude-skill&utm_campaign=web-builder), picks real cinematic media, writes a precise build spec, builds the page, then **screenshots its own work and fixes it** until it clears a gallery-level bar.

![Example designs from the skill, each next to the hero video it is built on](preview-media.jpg)
<sub>8 of the 40 example designs inside the skill, each shown next to the video it's built on. All 50+ videos are on the skill's media shelf.</sub>

## What's inside
- **40 example prompts:** the most-liked free prompts on MotionSites, the designs people actually love. Claude reads the closest 2–3 for every brief to match their level of detail and taste.
- **A media shelf:** 50+ cinematic hero videos, 30 transparent 3D cut-outs and 29 images, publicly hosted and shown on numbered contact sheets so Claude picks media by eye.
- **55+ technique recipes** with working code, for example:
  - seamless video loops;
  - liquid glass;
  - word-by-word blur headlines;
  - mouse-scrubbed video;
  - spotlight reveals;
  - depth carousels;
  - scroll stories;
  - real 3D models (Three.js).
- **Design taste rules with real numbers:** type scale, tracking, spacing, colour, motion timing and copy.
- **A spec template:** the precise brief Claude writes before coding. That's where quality is decided.
- **A look-and-fix loop:** a screenshot + QA script (broken assets, mobile overflow, fonts, video playback) and a scoring rubric.
- **Prompt mode:** ask for a prompt instead of code, and get one tuned for Lovable, Bolt, v0, Cursor, Manus, Google AI Studio or Kimi.

## Install

### Claude.ai and Claude desktop
1. Download **`motionsites-web-builder.zip`** from the [latest release](../../releases/latest).
2. In Claude, open **Customize → Skills → + → Create skill → Upload a skill**, choose the zip, and switch the skill on. (Code execution must be enabled in Settings → Capabilities.)

### Claude Code (plugin)
```
/plugin marketplace add Motionsites-AI/claude-skill
/plugin install motionsites-web-builder@motionsites
```
No GitHub SSH key? Use `/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Motionsites-AI/claude-skill.git` instead.

### Claude Code (manual)
Copy `plugins/motionsites-web-builder/skills/motionsites-web-builder` into `~/.claude/skills/`.

### Optional: let Claude see its work
The look-and-fix loop works best with Playwright:
```
pip install playwright && python -m playwright install chromium
```

# Halo

A minimal AI assistant that floats over your screen. It listens to the conversation, sees what's on your screen, and gives you a short suggestion in the moment: what to say or do. Halo is a from-scratch rewrite of the idea behind [sohzm/cheating-daddy](https://github.com/sohzm/cheating-daddy), with no bundler, no vendored libraries, and support for any OpenAI-compatible model.

![platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey) ![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--3.0-blue) ![deps](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-brightgreen)

## What's new

| | Cheating Daddy | Halo |
|---|---|---|
| Models | Gemini Live / Groq / OpenAI / local: four separate code paths | **One** OpenAI-compatible client: Gemini, Groq, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, or your own server |
| Speech | WebSocket stream to Gemini Live | VAD + Whisper-compatible API (Groq, OpenAI, or a local whisper.cpp / faster-whisper) |
| Screen | Screenshot on a timer | Continuous capture with a **change detector** and a rolling buffer of keyframes |
| Recording | None | Optional screen recording straight to disk as `.webm` |
| Security | `nodeIntegration: true`, no isolation | `contextIsolation`, `sandbox`, strict CSP, every IPC call validated, API keys encrypted by the OS |
| Code | ~11,700 lines plus vendored libraries | ~3,100 lines, 0 runtime dependencies, no build step |
| Tests | None | 27 unit tests (`npm test`) |

### New: Rewind ⏪(v 2.1)

Zoned out and lost the thread? Press **Ctrl+Shift+Enter** (or the button in the panel). Halo takes the transcript from the last 30 seconds to 5 minutes, plus a few screen keyframes, and answers in three lines:

- **What happened**: 2–3 bullets.
- **What they need from you now**: what exactly is being asked of you.
- **What to say**: a ready-made line.

Here's how it works:

```
getDisplayMedia ─▶ hidden <video> ─▶ every N ms: compare a 96×54 grayscale copy
       │                                      │
       │ (optional)                           ▼ did the screen change and then settle?
       └▶ MediaRecorder ─▶ .webm on disk      keyframe ─▶ Rewind buffer (3 min by default)
```

Only meaningful frames make it into the buffer: no duplicates, and nothing from the middle of an animation. The model gets a clean storyboard instead of a hundred identical screenshots. You can also **pin** frames in the Rewind panel, and they'll be sent along with your next question.

### Everything else

- **Two audio channels**: the other side (system audio) and you (microphone), labeled "Them" and "You". In "Both" mode, microphone lines are suppressed while the system channel has speech, so your speakers don't echo the other person under your name.
- **Auto-answer**: when Halo detects a question in the other side's speech, it prepares a suggestion on its own.
- **History and recaps**: every session is saved (transcript plus suggestions). The Recap button has the AI write a summary…

[Website and documentation](https://useraven.org) Raven runs Windows applications on Linux. You install them with their own installers, the same ones you would use on a PC, and they start: no virtual machine, no winetricks, no DLL overrides. The program's code runs directly on your CPU, inside a sandbox where it cannot reach Linux. Every call it makes to the system is answered by Raven, which plays the part of the Windows kernel and its services: processes and threads, files, the registry, windows and input. Graphics go to Wayland and Vulkan, with DXVK and vkd3d-proton for Direct3D. ## Requirements - Linux on x86_64 - CMake 3.20 or newer, a C++20 compiler and Python 3.11 or newer - MinGW-w64 for x86_64 and i686, to build the Windows test programs - For desktop applications: Wayland, xkbcommon, pixman, FreeType and Vulkan - Optionally, for the experimental X11 desktop: libxcb with its xkb, xfixes and xinput extensions, and xkbcommon-x11 The tested setup also uses libpng 1.6.59, a CPU build of Skia with the Liberation fonts, DXVK and vkd3d-proton; the `scripts/provision-*.py` tools download the pinned versions. ## Installation Raven is built from source for now: ```sh git clone https://github.com/mirkobrombin/raven.git cd raven cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo cmake --build build -j2 ``` Then run an installer, or any program: ```sh export RAVEN_PREFIX="$HOME/.local/share/raven/my-app" build/native/raven --run-process --execution=native --timeout-ms=600000 --desktop=wayland setup.exe ``` This minimal build runs console programs and simple windows. Installers and most desktop programs also need the common controls, the shell dialogs and the installer services, which Raven builds from pinned ReactOS sources, for both 64-bit and 32-bit programs. Without them a program stops at its first call into them, such as `InitCommonControls`: ```sh python3 scripts/provision-rtl.py --output components/rtl python3 scripts/provision-controls.py --output components/controls python3 scripts/provision-controls.py --arch x86 --output components/controls32 python3 scripts/provision-installer.py --output components/installer python3 scripts/provision-installer.py --arch x86 --output components/installer32 python3 scripts/provision-graphics.py --destination components/graphics cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \ -DRAVEN_RTL_COMPONENT_PATH=$PWD/components/rtl/raven-rtl.dll \ -DRAVEN_CONTROLS_COMPONENT_DIR=$PWD/components/controls -DRAVEN_CONTROLS32_COMPONENT_DIR=$PWD/components/controls32 \ -DRAVEN_INSTALLER_COMPONENT_DIR=$PWD/components/installer -DRAVEN_INSTALLER32_COMPONENT_DIR=$PWD/components/installer32 \ -DRAVEN_DXVK_PE64_DIR=$PWD/components/graphics/dxvk/pe64 -DRAVEN_DXVK_PE32_DIR=$PWD/components/graphics/dxvk/pe32 \ -DRAVEN_VKD3D_PE64_DIR=$PWD/components/graphics…

lovisdotio/video-to-game.content:
# Video to Game A skill that teaches coding agents to turn a gameplay video into a real game you can play in the browser. A video model designs the game (its look, camera and one memorable mechanic); the agent studies the clip frame by frame, generates every image, 3D model and sound with fal to match it, writes the game in Three.js, then plays it with the keyboard and films its best seconds as proof. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and others. **Play the 31 games:** [fal-video-to-game.vercel.app](https://fal-video-to-game.vercel.app) ![Video to Game: the generated video shrinks, the code and the fal assets come in, the game appears](gallery/hero.gif) 31 original games, every one rebuilt from a 10 to 15 s video generated with MiniMax H3 Max on fal: 1,013 fal calls (594 images, 194 3D models, 290 sounds and music tracks), 202 USD in total, about 6 USD per game. Every game is a single `index.html` with Three.js and nothing else: no engine, no template, no other library. ## Why Agents cannot design a game's look. Asked for "a game where a boy glides between flying whales", they ship grey boxes, a default sky and a camera that fights the player. A video model is good at exactly that part, so let it go first, and make the agent match it: - **The video is the design document.** `study_video.py` turns it into frames, a contact sheet, a palette and cut times; the agent writes a spec (camera, hero, the one mechanic, the key moment, the look) from named frames. - **Every asset comes from fal, from the video's own frames.** Concept sheets with Nano Banana Pro, clean cutouts, image to 3D (Meshy, Tripo, Hunyuan 3D), rigging and animations, sound effects and music, all logged with `fal_asset.py`. Nothing drawn by hand, nothing downloaded. - **The look is a spec, not polish.** Tone mapping, one grade, fog, bloom, vignette and grain from the first scene, and a side-by-side picture of the video and the game at the same three spots after every change. - **Calm the world so the game reads.** One harmonized palette, dense but grouped, the hero and everything you can interact with standing out on a quiet background. No text on screen. - **The agent plays its own game.** A keyboard scenario reads `window.__game` like a player reads the screen, `record_play.mjs` films it at the real frame rate, `best_window.py` finds the liveliest seconds. Falls, walls and dead seconds get fixed before anyone else plays. ## The gallery Each GIF is the generated video (left) and the game (right). soimy/c3rb3r-rescue.content:
# c3rb3r-rescue

一次 DSM / GitLab 勒索事件的取证、内存密钥恢复和副本解密记录。目标是让下一次处置能够复现经过验证的步骤，同时保留失败和证据缺口。

本工具适用于已分析的 `libgld` 样本与文件格式，**不是 C3RB3R 家族的通用解密器**。样本 SHA-256：`802ac85d19dc6db2b1849bb3499877280544d04a0ae94d4c408b6c321669903d`。不包含恶意二进制、业务数据或可运行的入侵载荷。

**现按所有者授权公开一份真实的 [48 字节会话恢复候选](profiles/recovery-key-20261028.json)**，供其他受害者在副本上验证。它来自 RAM，不是攻击者的 RSA 私钥；只验证过本事件的文件，**没有跨受害者成功证据**。相同攻击者、样本或后缀不代表密钥相同。适用范围、导出命令和匹配方法见[密钥说明](docs/key-sharing.md)。

**首要目标是保住仍在内存中的解密材料。** 在阻止继续加密并保留管理通道后，尽早采集可取得的进程内存和整机 RAM；不要等全盘盘点、漏洞归因或完整反编译做完才 dump。不要为清理恶意程序先 kill、重启、升级系统或启动另一张救援盘。内存采集不能保证一定有可用密钥，但失去这份易失证据后，本案的恢复路径可能不再成立。

本案成功来自 **PVE 来宾 RAM**。新增的[物理机 Linux / DSM 采集指南](skills/dsm-ransomware-rescue/references/physical-memory.md)覆盖进程映射、AVML 和 LiME；物理 DSM 整机采集尚未实机验收，不能把本次 VM 成功外推到所有设备。

## 交给 AI 使用

可把仓库 URL 和下面这段任务说明交给助手；先提供系统/架构、是否仍开机、可用管理通道和现有授权范围，**不要发送密码、真实密钥、完整内存或业务文件**：

> 阅读 README 与 skills/dsm-ransomware-rescue/SKILL.md。以保住易失密钥为优先，确认当前机器是虚拟机还是物理机，区分进程内存和整机 RAM。先调查可用权限、暂停状态、目标存储和采集兼容性，再在现有授权内采取适用的步骤。保留原始文件、独立副本和校验收据；不要执行样本、自动加载不匹配的内核模块或重启受灾机。只对副本尝试解密，分别报告已验证结果、猜测和未覆盖范围。

症状相同不证明样本、会话或密钥相同。当前解密器还检查本案会话尾标记；其他事件须重新验证布局及标记，不能通过删除校验强行运行。参见[密钥复用与分享](docs/key-sharing.md)。

本次结果：16 GiB 内存副本中找到可用的 48 字节主材料；五组已知明密文逐字节一致。10/24 的约 49 GiB 周备份与历史摘要一致，随后在隔离的同版本 GitLab 中恢复出 80 个项目、23 个用户、16 个群组和 9253 个 LFS 对象。仓库、secrets、LFS、附件和 artifacts 检查通过，登录页返回 200。10/22 的另一份周备份存在交错重复加密，仍未完整恢复。新发现的内存日志高可信指向 DSM 登录插件环境注入、与 CVE-2024-10441 一致，尚缺少完整请求和执行链。

## 阅读入口

- [事件过程与证据边界](docs/incident-report.md)
- [攻击路径：日志、RAM 结构与漏洞判断](docs/attack-path.md) · [可复核证据索引](docs/attack-path-evidence.json)
- [封存布局、保管和重验](docs/evidence-seal.md)
- [工具验证记录](docs/toolkit-validation.md)
- [物理机采集与失败分流](skills/dsm-ransomware-rescue/references/physical-memory.md)
- [密钥层级、复用与公开边界](docs/key-sharing.md)
- [可复用 skill](skills/dsm-ransomware-rescue/SKILL.md)：保全、RAM、REA 逆向、盘点、解密、GitLab 验收。

## 本地与 GitHub 的边界

GitHub 仓库公开，保存脱敏记录、skill、源码、合成测试、样本布局参数，以及上述单独授权的恢复候选。每次发布仍检查 Git 暂存区；该授权不涵盖其他密钥、账号凭据、完整 RAM 或业务数据。

`private/` 被 Git 忽略，保存本机证据副本、内存 dump、其余密钥候选、原始日志、对话快照和保管清单。**Git clone 包含单独发布的候选，但不包含这些私有证据，也不能重建其他会话的密钥。** 大体积业务密文和恢复备份仍在救援 NAS，位置和既有校验收据由本地索引记录，不复制到 Git 历史。

这是逻辑封存：独立副本、逐文件摘要、落盘重读、只读权限和来源记录。没有做全盘取证镜像，没有将运行中的 DSM 变为不可变磁盘快照，也没有将联网 NAS 称为离线备份。

## 使用

工具目录：`skills/dsm-ransomware-rescue/scripts/`。分析环境 Python 3.11+；实际回归环境为 Python 3.12，NumPy / cryptography 版本见 `requirements.txt`。DSM 元数据盘点和新增进程采集器只需标准库 Python 3.8+；不要为了运行解密器升级受灾系统。

在干净的分析机建立环境：

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
PYTHONPATH=skills/dsm-ransomware-rescue/scripts:scripts .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
.venv/bin/python skills/dsm-ransomware-rescue/scripts/verify_backup.py --self-test
```

单文件解密，输入必须是独立密文副本，输出必须不存在：

```sh
.venv/bin/python skills/dsm-ransomware-rescue/scripts/decrypt_copy.py \
  --copy-root /analysis/copies \
  --input-copy /analysis/copies/example.tar.L0CK3D \
  --master-file /analysis/private/master.bin \
  --output /analysis/recovered/example.tar \
  --expected-sha256 KNOWN_ORIGINAL_SHA2…

# /carrossel

Skill para Claude Code e Codex que cria carrosséis com a cara da sua marca: do roteiro ao PNG em 2x, com galeria, slider, comparação de versões e legenda pronta.

![Prompt solto vs. /carrossel](docs/antes-depois.png)

## Por que não é "só um prompt"

O que deixa um carrossel bom não é o prompt, é o processo:

1. **Roteiro antes do visual.** A IA propõe a copy slide a slide e só desenha depois do seu ok.
2. **A galeria é a referência.** Cada peça aprovada vira referência para a próxima, então o estilo se mantém.
3. **Assets próprios.** Uma série de imagens no estilo da marca, gerada com image gen a partir de uma âncora aprovada.
4. **Checagem visual.** Cada slide é renderizado e conferido antes de chegar em você.
5. **Gosto acumulado.** Toda recusa ou aprovação vai para um `GOSTO.md`, que a skill lê antes de cada peça. Quanto mais você usa, mais ela acerta.

## Funciona para

- **Marca que já existe:** a skill lê seu site, logo e posts e monta o manual a partir deles.
- **Marca do zero:** faz algumas perguntas, propõe 2 ou 3 direções e monta a identidade com você.

## O que você recebe

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Galeria](docs/galeria.png) | ![Slider](docs/slider.png) |
| **Galeria** com todas as peças e versões | **Slider** com legenda, comparação e download em alta |

Cada slide sai em HTML editável, PNG 1080×1350 e PNG 2160×2700.

Vídeo de 24s: [`docs/motion/lancamento.mp4`](docs/motion/lancamento.mp4)

## Instalação

Requer Node 18+.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/guilhermealvestech/carrossel-skill
cp -r carrossel-skill/skills/carrossel ~/.claude/skills/carrossel   # Claude Code
cp -r carrossel-skill/skills/carrossel ~/.codex/skills/carrossel    # Codex

# Survival LLM

A free AI assistant and survival library that runs entirely on your own computer and works with no
internet. Ask it how to keep food safe in a blackout, treat a burn or purify water: it searches an
offline library of medical, emergency, how-to and encyclopedia articles, answers from what it finds,
and shows you the exact passage each answer came from.

- **Offline and private.** The AI model and the library live on your computer. Your questions never leave it, and once set up it works with the internet off.
- **Shows its sources.** Every answer lists the articles it read; click one to read it yourself, cited passage highlighted, with its license. Ask "where did you get that?" and it opens the source.
- **Shows its reasoning.** Show reasoning, under each answer, opens what the AI thought before it answered, step by step, with the searches and articles it read in between. It stays hidden until you click it. How much it reasons is up to you: Reasoning, next to Send, is a budget (Off, 1,000, 4,000 or 16,000 tokens, or no limit), and at the limit its thinking stops and it answers from what it has.
- **Yours to adjust.** The Instructions button shows the instructions the AI gets before you ask anything (the app adds today's date, the names of your files and your Memory notes after them); edit them and Save to change how it answers (Reset brings back the original). The Length limit next to Send sets how long an answer may run, or turns the limit off.
- **Add your own files.** Your files, at the top, takes PDFs, Word documents, EPUB ebooks, web pages and text files (drop them on the window or choose them), so the AI can search your generator's manual, your medicines list or your family's emergency plan along with the library. They stay on your computer, in the `Survival LLM Files` folder in your home folder; files you put in that folder, or change there, are picked up on their own. It can't read scans or photos of pages yet.
- **Remembers you.** Tell it your daughter is allergic to penicillin or that you have a Honda generator, and it saves a short note so later chats know it too; each answer shows what it saved, with Undo. Memory, at the top, shows every note in one list you can edit, and a switch turns off the AI's saving (it still reads the notes you keep). The notes stay on your computer, in one plain text file with the app's settings.
- **Updates itself.** Check for updates, at the bottom of the window, looks for a new version (it also looks once a day while it runs, by fetching one small file from the project's web page; nothing about you is sent). Update now downloads it, checks it, and restarts into it, keeping your models, library, files and settings. Newer libraries are offered there too.

# OunceCake

(`ozdumptool` if you're ***lame*** and ***boring***) 

Tool to dump unencrypted romFS and exeFS for Switch 2 games, updates and DLC.

Supports digital games, game cards, Switch 2 Editions, etc.

## Disclaimer

For the love of God, do NOT share any files you rip using this tool. It is to be used with ONLY your own games on your OWN system. This tool doesn't provide system keys or any method to decrypt files. The files are loaded normally by the system, then pulled over FTP.

## Usage

0. Take note of your Switch 2's local IP address. It can be found in the network settings.

1. Clone the repo: 
``` 
git clone https://github.com/misshexa66/OunceCake.git
```

2. Use kurumuz's fork of the [ns2jb exploit](https://gitlab.com/kurumuz/ns2jb) to get an RPC connection with the system. Use `node run.cjs --rpc`.

3. Run `node ouncecake.cjs <path-to-ns2jb-run>`. The output from ns2jb will tell you where this path is. (`Run folder: /home/hexa/projects/ns2jb2/runs/switch2-Icu7Jd`)

4. OunceCake will prompt you to pick a game. Pick one, then wait.

5. When OunceCake says `FTP up! ftp://<switch 2 ip>:2121`, use an FTP client to connect to your Switch 2's local IP address with port 2121. A username and password is not required. (Make sure your FTP client has its transfer mode set to Binary/Image/TYPE I.)

## Licensing

OunceCake is licensed under the terms of the GPLv2 (because it borrows a tiny bit of code from [Atmosphere](https://github.com/Atmosphere-NX/Atmosphere))

You can find a copy of the license in the LICENSE file.

# DeepOpen-3d-webs

中文  [中文说明](https://github.com/deepopen-com/deepopen-3d-webs/blob/main/README-cn.md)


# Project Overview

Guangyu Zaojing (光域造景) is an image-driven 3D scene generation system. You supply one reference image and a prompt, and the system generates scene results along a camera trajectory that you can preview, replay, and trace. The official 3D demo assets play color/depth animations and Gaussian point clouds directly in the browser. The web app ships as a Docker image and listens on port `8090` by default.

![Guangyu Zaojing workbench](docs/user/images/ScreenShot_2026-10-19_201426_816.png)

## 1. Background and Goals

A single image rarely turns into spatial content you can look around in, move through, and hand off. The traditional pipeline splits depth estimation, image completion, 3D representation, and camera flythrough across separate tools, so creators can't carry a scene from start to finish in one interface.

Guangyu Zaojing collapses that chain into a single studio:

- Describe a scene with a reference image and a Chinese prompt
- Use a generation trajectory to decide how the space is observed, and a render trajectory to decide how the final footage moves
- Produce preview stills, color animations, and depth animations; bake Gaussians on the fly with full compute, or mount the official demo PLY directly
- Drag to preview point clouds in the browser, and download complete models for SuperSplat / MeshLab
- Every task is persisted, so you can later "View & Demo" it by ID

The system runs in demo mode by default. Without a GPU, the pages, the gallery's 3D demos, and task replay all remain usable. With CUDA and model weights available, you can switch to the full 3D generation engine.

## 2. Use Cases

- **Spatial concept design**: Get a look-around version of an interior, building, or natural landscape before deciding whether to invest in refinement
- **Stylized content**: Anime, fantasy, holiday, and post-apocalyptic presets load in directly — well suited to style exploration
- **Design reviews**: Put stills, flythrough footage, and point-cloud previews on one page for collaborators
- **Teaching and demos**: Demo mode needs no GPU; the official `demo-*` assets work well in classrooms and pitch sessions
- **A starting point for 3D assets**: Export PLY Gaussian point clouds for downstream viewing or processing

## 3. Core Features

The system has five tabs.

**Workbench**

Summarizes total tasks, completed and failed counts, sample scene count, run mode, CUDA, disk, host, and service port. Click "Refresh System Data" to re-collect.

**Scene Generation**

- Upload a reference image, or load an image, positive/negative prompts, model, seed, steps, and camera trajectory from a Chinese example
- Diffusion model options: the standard SD1.5, Blazing Drive V11m, Realistic Vision V5.1, Cartoon Pixar V5
- Generation trajectories: Look Around, Overhead Orbit, Spin in Place 360
- Render trajectories: Push In and Out, Classic Orbit, Subtl…

# 复旦大学期中期末往年卷（按科目、老师整理）

把网上公开分享的复旦期中、期末卷集中到一起，按 **科目 → 老师** 两层整理，方便按自己老师找卷子复习。

> **版权说明**：试卷的版权归出题教师、复旦大学和原整理者所有。本仓库只做收集和分类，仅供学习交流，**禁止商用、禁止售卖**。
> 如果你是版权所有者，或者认为某份文件不应公开，请提 Issue，会尽快删除。

## 目录结构

```
科目/
  拼音缩写_老师全名/    例如 fh_冯辉
  统考/                全校统一命题（高数、线代期末，大物 B 期末，思政，军理，生导，基物实验，Python 等）
  佚名/                找不到老师的
```

- 科目名是“大类-课名”，例如 `数学-线性代数`、`物理-大学物理B下`。
- 只收期中、期末卷（含期末回忆版、答案、讲评）。小测、模拟卷、题库、课件、笔记都没有收。
- 数学分析 B 的“阶段性考试”保留了（谢锡麟班用它代替期中）。
- 加密 PDF 的密码写在文件名里。
- `*_考题回忆(Notion题库).md` 是学生考后回忆的题目文字。

带 **[猜]** 的卷子，老师是推测的，不是卷上写的。2020 年以前、只按页面归属归给某位老师的旧卷也标了 [猜]。主要依据：

simpsoka/zigzag.content: # ZigZag ZigZag is a visual embroidery editor built in Rust for performance, with built-in **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** support so AI agents can create and edit designs alongside you. Turn SVG artwork into stitches, fine-tune it in the editor, and export **PES, DST, EXP, JEF, or VP3** for broad compatibility with embroidery machines—or send designs directly to a **Brother Skitch (PP1) over Bluetooth**. Draw in Illustrator, draw in ZigZag, or let an agent draw. The Rust engine and `zigzag` command-line tool power the same workflow outside the editor. ## Download for Mac **[Download ZigZag.dmg](https://github.com/simpsoka/zigzag/releases/latest/download/ZigZag.dmg)** For Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, macOS 11 or later. Open the DMG, then drag ZigZag into Applications. The release is signed and notarized by Apple. No Rust installation is needed. [Release notes and checksums](https://github.com/simpsoka/zigzag/releases/latest) · [Publishing a release](RELEASE.md) ``` zigzag/ src/svg.rs SVG import (usvg): fill and stroke parts, transforms, text src/document/ editable document; settings saved back into SVG ids, layout edits as SVG transforms, lettering src/params.rs stitch settings tokens + fabric presets src/stitch/fill.rs tatami fill (scanline sections, staggered rows) src/stitch/satin.rs satin columns: two rails, auto-satin, underlays, short stitches src/stitch/stroke.rs running / triple-run stitch src/boolean.rs polygon booleans and offsets (i_overlay) src/design.rs planner: overlap removal, cap order, routing, trims src/checks.rs digitizing checks (sizes, widths, lettering, hoop) src/formats/ PES (+PEC), DST, EXP, JEF, VP3, Skitch PEN writers; PES/PEC/DST/EXP/JEF readers; preview; worksheet src/machine/ Skitch Bluetooth protocol (+ btleplug client, `ble` feature) src/studio/ editor (egui on OpenGL via glow) + MCP server (`gui` feature) src/mcp_bridge.rs stdio ↔ HTTP bridge for MCP clients that launch a command ``` ## Build ```sh cargo build --release # CLI + MCP bridge, no system deps cargo build --release --features gui,ble # + the studio editor and Skitch upload ``` Linux needs the usual X11/Wayland and OpenGL dev libraries for `gui`. libdbus is vendored for `ble`. ## Stitch types | Type | What it does | Works on | |---|---|---| | **Fill** (tatami) | Staggered rows, any angle, with underlay (edge walk + rows) and pull compensation | Filled shapes | | **Satin** | Zigzag column between two rails, with center/contour/zigzag underlay, pull compensation and short stitches on tight curves; plain, S-stitch or zig-zag top stitching; several threads across the column (multicolor satin) | Strokes (any width); Ink/Stitch-sty…

aschmelyun/print-my-profile-pic.content: # print-my-profile-pic Star this repo to have your GitHub profile picture framed, printed out on my receipt printer, and stuck to my wall. That's it! > [!TIP] > If you give a one-time [sponsorship](https://github.com/sponsors/aschmelyun?frequency=one-time&sponsor=aschmelyun) of any amount beforehand, your profile picture will be printed in a **special frame**. ## How's it work? GitHub allows you to create webhooks for specific events on your repos, I've set one up for [starring](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#star) this project. When that happens, a payload is POSTed to a [Cloudflare tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/) domain, which leads to a PHP script running on a Raspberry Pi that's sitting on my desk. From the inbound request, you can gleen info about the person who starred the repo, like their display name and avatar URL. The script takes their profile picture, renders it behind a cut-out of a photo frame, and then adds some other info I thought should be included in each receipt. The RPi is connected to an Epson TM-T88IV thermal receipt printer via USB, and the PHP script uses my go-to [escpos-php](https://github.com/mike42/escpos-php) library to format the receipt data and send it off to the printer. ## But why? It sounded fun when my friend [Sam](https://x.com/samwhoo) mentioned it. That's pretty much it! ## What now? I'll periodically update this README with a picture of the pinboard I've dubbed the "Hall of Frame" as pictures get added to it. Want to add a new frame? Send in a PR!

# TotK Recomp

**TotK Recomp** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native Windows x86-64 application ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of *Tears of the Kingdom*, dumped from your own console: the base game and the 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided.
>
> The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it.

## Status

Early development. The game is playable on Windows; visual bugs and crashes are still expected.

Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Features

- Native code, not emulation
- Game updates 1.2.1 and 1.4.3, with saves that carry over between them
- 60 fps by default; up to 144 fps or the monitor's refresh rate (experimental)
- Custom resolutions (1080p, 2k...), supersampling and AMD FSR 1 upscaling
- In-game settings menu (F1) and performance overlay (F10)
- Keyboard, mouse and gamepad with remapping, rumble and gyro
- Shaders prepared at install instead of during play

## Planned

- Linux and the Steam Deck
- Mods made for emulators: unpack a mod into a `mods` folder
- Custom aspect ratios, including ultrawide
- VRR

## Installing

Requirements: Windows 10 or later, an x86-64 CPU with AVX2, a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and `VK_EXT_external_memory_host`, about 36 GiB free during setup (20 GiB after).

1. Download `TotK-Setup-<version>-windows.zip` from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and unpack it.
2. Start `TotK-Setup.exe`. If SmartScreen warns about an unsigned app, choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
3. Pick your game files, the language and an install folder, and press *Start*. The setup builds the game once.
4. Play `totk.exe` from the install folder.

To update, run a newer `TotK-Setup.exe` on the same folder; saves and settings are kept. Settings are in the in-game menu and in `totk.ini` ([totk.ini.example](totk.ini.example) lists every key). Controls: [docs/controls.md](docs/controls.md).

## Credits

TotK Recomp builds on the projects below. What was taken from each, with its license, is listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

- [LAS Recomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp)
- [MacNativeGames](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames)
- [d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile) and [nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)
- [SavageWindRecomp](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp)
- [Ryujinx](https://github.com/Ryujinx/Ryujinx)
- [deko3d](https://github.com/devkitPro/deko3d)

# Zeabur **Simple, secure deployments on your own Kubernetes.** Zeabur is an open-source platform you host yourself. It runs in your cluster (or on your machine), shows the cluster as projects and services, explains what is wrong in plain words, and lets you change things safely. It works with the objects you already have, never acts with more rights than you have, and keeps no state of its own: no database, no custom resources. **[oss.zeabur.com/zeabur](https://oss.zeabur.com/zeabur/)** shows what Zeabur does, and **[the documentation](https://oss.zeabur.com/docs/zeabur/)** covers installing, deploying, configuring and operating the cluster, and leaving Zeabur, in English, [繁體中文](https://oss.zeabur.com/zh-TW/docs/zeabur/) and [简体中文](https://oss.zeabur.com/zh-CN/docs/zeabur/). > **Status: pre-alpha (0.1.1).** The API may still change, and it has been tried on few > clusters. Do not point it at a cluster you cannot afford to break.

# Subvox

A macOS prototype that tests whether AirPods Pro head-motion data (`CMHeadphoneMotionManager`) carries enough information to turn **silently mouthed words into text**.

It doesn't use a language model. It's a small-vocabulary template recognizer plus a statistical test that tells you whether the signal is real.

## Build & run

```sh
brew install xcodegen   # once
xcodegen generate
open Subvox.xcodeproj   # ⌘R
```

Or from the command line:

```sh
xcodebuild -project Subvox.xcodeproj -scheme Subvox -derivedDataPath build -allowProvisioningUpdates build
open build/Build/Products/Debug/Subvox.app
xcodebuild -project Subvox.xcodeproj -scheme Subvox -derivedDataPath build test
```

Requires macOS 14+, AirPods Pro or another headphone that supports head tracking, connected as the Mac's audio output. On first launch, grant **Motion**. The mic and speech prompts only appear when you start the mic.

## Screens

| Screen | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Sensors** | Live plots of user acceleration, rotation rate and attitude, the measured sample rate, a mic input picker and level meter, and a recorder for experiment sessions. |
| **Train** | Pick a word, hold **Space**, mouth it, release. Each take is stored as a template. **Evaluate** runs leave-one-out classification and a 500× label-permutation test, then shows accuracy against chance, a p-value and a confusion matrix. The feature checkboxes (acceleration / rotation / attitude) let you test which channels carry the signal. |
| **Decode** | The motion-to-text screen. Hold Space, or use auto-detect after calibrating the noise floor. Each segment is DTW-matched against your templates and added to the transcript. A live mic transcript runs alongside it for comparison. |

## How decoding works

1. **Segmentation** (`CaptureController`). Space-hold, or an energy trigger above a calibrated noise floor with pre-roll and hangover.
2. **Features** (`MotionFeatures`). Per frame: user acceleration (3), rotation rate (3), and attitude change since the start of the segment (3). Each channel is mean-centered, and quiet lead-in and lead-out frames are trimmed.
3. **Matching** (`DTW`, `TemplateClassifier`). Each channel is z-scaled across the training set. Matching is 1-nearest-neighbour per word, using dynamic time warping with a Sakoe–Chiba band. A segment is rejected if the best distance is above *max distance* or the margin to the runner-up is below *min confidence*.
4. **Is it real?** (`Evaluation`). The leave-one-out accuracy is compared with the same procedure run on shuffled labels. If p < 0.05, the motion stream distinguishes your words better than chance.

## Experiment protocol

Use **Record Session** in the toolbar or on the Sensors screen. Recordings go to `~/Documents/Subvox/Sessions/<timestamp>-<condition>/`:

- `motion.csv`: every motion sample. `t` is seconds from session start.
- `audio.caf`: microphone audio, if the mic is running.
- `events.csv`: every Space-held segment, with its label or pr…

# DrewLevin Detector

A League of Legends match-history tool with a sense of humor. Enter a Riot ID,
get a Drew Index, and open **THE RECEIPTS** to inspect the matches behind each
detected change.

Live site: [drewed.lol](https://drewed.lol/)

## What it does

- Reviews every Solo/Duo and Flex match returned for the current year and the
  previous two years, with paginated history requests.
- Compares Flash placement, item slots, rune pages, champion and role habits,
  and sustained performance changes across that history.
- Keeps Solo/Duo and Flex performance comparisons separate while comparing
  mechanical habits across both queues.
- Shows dated evidence, baseline comparisons, match IDs, participant details,
  and complete rune pages in dialogs.
- Provides a scan queue, progress updates, cached match details, and local game
  assets.

Supported platforms: **NA1, BR1, LA1, LA2, EUW1, EUN1, TR1**.

The Drew Index is a heuristic score derived from the available match history.
Coverage depends on the matches the upstream services still return. OP.GG and
Rewind can supplement historical rank labels or totals; those aggregates do
not supply the individual matches used as evidence.

## Run locally

Requirements: Node.js **22.13 or newer**, npm, and one
[Riot API key](https://developer.riotgames.com/).

```sh
npm ci
```

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in the single server-side variable:

```dotenv
RIOT_API_KEY=
```

```sh
npm run dev
```

Open [localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173). The key is used only by server-side
API routes. Keep `.env.local` private; Git and Docker builds exclude it.
Restart the application after replacing the token.

For UI previews without Riot requests, use `/?preview=low` or `/?preview=queue`.

## API requests and pacing

All Riot calls go through `lib/riot.ts` and use **one** `RIOT_API_KEY`. Requests
to each routing host share a queue, with a 1.3-second minimum interval between
starts. A 429 response pauses that queue according to `Retry-After`. Temporary
network and server failures receive up to three attempts; a rejected token
returns an error.

The application processes one account scan at a time per running instance.
Analysis results are cached in memory for a short time, and match details are
cached in memory for up to 24 hours. Queue and cache ownership assume a single
application instance. The KV binding stores the counter and progress updates.

## Checks

```sh
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run check:secrets
npm run build
```

Tests use deterministic upstream responses and a virtual clock. They do not
need an API key or call Riot. The secret check scans Git's tracked and untracked
publishable files without printing matched secret values.

## Docker

Create `.env.local` as above, then run:

```sh
docker compose -f compose.production.yml up -d --build
```

The service listens on `127.0.0.1:4173`. Compose mounts the environment file as a

# RAN Sentinel

An AI co-engineer for mobile networks, built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon.

RAN Sentinel watches a cluster of LTE cells in Seattle, WA (US bands B66, B2 and B71) and spots a degrading cell. Muse Spark agents investigate it with read-only tools and propose a fix. Fixed safety rules and a digital twin check that fix before anyone sees it. The recommendation then goes to the right department. When a configuration change is approved, it is sent as an Open M-Plane change package with automatic rollback, and the cell is watched until it recovers. Customers of the fictional operator **Northstar Connect** see only confirmed, plain-language updates.

Everything runs on a **simulated** network. Nothing here connects to a real operator.

**New since 2026-10-30:** a verified investigation built on the patterns in Meta's
[legal-agent workshop](https://github.com/meta-models/legal-agent-workshop). Every diagnosis passes a verifier the agents cannot skip.
The agent pauses to ask a field engineer when the data cannot settle a cause. It keeps a living plan, works one tool per turn and
resumes from its last step after an API failure, and an engineer signs off the root cause
([details](docs/VERIFIED_INVESTIGATION.md)). Customers also get a hands-free **voice agent** that operates the app
([details](docs/VOICE_AGENT.md)).

**Hackathon entry:** Indie track, theme "Build for Your World". The submission summary is in [SUBMISSION.md](SUBMISSION.md), the 3-minute demo script is in [DEMO.md](DEMO.md), and the code is MIT-licensed ([LICENSE](LICENSE)).

|---|---|
| Impact (30%) | Cuts the time from a degrading cell to a safe, approved fix for small carrier ops teams; tracks FCC Part 4 duty; keeps customers informed |
| Use of Meta AI tooling (25%) | Six Meta models, each with one job: Muse Spark 1.3/1.2/1.1, Muse Wonder 1.0, SAM 3.1 and Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0, plus Open M-Plane and Maveric; the investigation follows Meta's legal-agent workshop patterns |
| Demo (25%) | Live fault injection from the console; red-team, twin outage, diagnostics outage and model outage switches show every safety path; a customer voice agent |
| Technical depth (20%) | Six layers, five bounded loops, a diagnosis verifier, nine safety rules, checkpoints and resume, NETCONF confirmed-commit with rollback, detector benchmarked on TelecomTS, 120 automated tests |

- **FCC Part 4 outage check** (47 CFR 4.9(e)). # Span

Span implements a branch relaxing assembler in Isabelle/HOL, with proofs of termination, minimum layout size and execution correspondence for a bytecode machine with signed 8-bit and 16-bit relative branches

[![](media/demo.gif)](media/demo.mp4)

## Correctness

An overflowing short branch must be wide in every valid assignment. [Relaxation](Relax.thy) computes the least widening set terminating on the number of remaining short branches. A final range check decides whether any valid layout exists

[Encoding](Encoding.thy) proves byte bounds and decoder inversion and [Execution correspondence](Machine.thy) relates source execution `S` and bytecode execution `B` through relocation `R` for every fuel bound (including suspended states)

![](media/correspondence.svg)

Minimality assumes fixed instruction order and excludes alignment directives while the machine uses a natural valued accumulator and biased little endian branch payloads. The execution theorem starts from resolved instructions and excludes the SML compiler, runtime and OS I/O

# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want, or just ask in your own words and Claude picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield. If none is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server, and it shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation. Dashboards and apps rarely need one.
- **Story video.** A square video under 10 seconds of your screen unslopping itself, ready to post. It needs Playwright and ffmpeg.

Try it on the two vibecoded screens in [examples](examples).

## Hire the unslopper

Would rather have a designer do it? Damir unslops one key screen in 3 days, built in your stack, at [heydamir.design/unslop](https://heydamir.design/unslop).

## License

# Git for Global Law

**The world's law in one git history. Every word traced to the law that wrote it for any country and any date.**

An expansion of the same for the US Code, [#1 on Hacker News (28/10/26)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50268380).
Semantic, searchable law on a global scale.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f24f3411-24d9-416a-8c45-9cebc817c64e

**Free to use: [CC0](LICENSE.md).** Fork it, build on it, ship it in a product: no permission or credit needed. The law text
sits in each country's repository, under that repository's own terms.

The law of many jurisdictions as one git history. Each jurisdiction's law is its own repository, where every commit
is one law taking effect, written by that law. This repository arranges those repositories by jurisdiction and
interleaves their histories in the order the changes took force, so a single commit here is the state of all of them on
one day.

```
global-law/
├── manifest.json            every corpus: path, source repo, coverage, which trailer holds the in-force date
├── jurisdiction.json        the world, and its children: 193 UN members, other territories with their own ISO code, and the EU
├── germany/                 Germany (ISO code DE in its jurisdiction.json)
│   ├── SOURCES.md           where German law can be read, with what each source offers
│   └── bund/                federal law
│       └── acts/            submodule: the Grundgesetz since 1949 (grundgesetz/), every other federal act since 2019
├── estonia/                 Estonia
│   └── national/acts/       submodule: Estonia's law history, from its corpus.json
├── france/                  France: jurisdiction.json and SOURCES.md, no history yet
└── …                        every other country, the same way
```

Each country's law lives in its own repository, `lexifina/<country>-law`, which says where it belongs here in a
`corpus.json` at its root. A country whose repository still holds only its sources (no law yet) has a folder with its
`jurisdiction.json` and `SOURCES.md`, and no submodule: only real law is pinned. Laws adopted but not yet in force stay
on each corpus's future branch; `main` here holds only what is in force by the build date.

Corpora differ widely in reach. Some hold a country's whole statute book (Czechia, Spain, Switzerland, Georgia, Malta);
others hold a few acts, or a sample: the US corpus is nine titles of the United States Code, and the UK corpus is the
special educational needs law. `manifest.json` gives each corpus's `coverage`, and `history` says how its past is known:
`in-force` (dated official versions), `replayed` (rebuilt by applying each amending act; its `verification` says which
dates were checked) or `current-only` (today's text only).

## Using it from an AI model (MCP)

`tools/mcp_server.py` is a Model Context Protocol server for this tree. It lets Claude or any other MCP client ask the

kevinraymond/florilegium.content: # florilegium ## Origin The [Reddit post](https://www.reddit.com/r/LaTeX/comments/1xixznw/how_do_you_make_these_flowers_in_latex/) asked how to make flowers like these in LaTeX. I don't know how the original was made, and this project doesn't try to reproduce it. It is one possible way, and the way I did it: hand-authored primitives with randomized parameters, painted in Lua, placed by a procedural layout whose "fill the unused space" part borrows a 1998 idea from the ornament literature. It gets a similar look. ## What it is Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LaTeX. No images, no imported paths, no external assets: every petal, leaf and stem is a parametric curve computed in Lua while the page is being written, painted like a watercolor, and written straight into the PDF. Every page gets its own garden. ![six seeds](gallery/seeds.gif) *Six seeds of the grown composition. Same code, different seed — and the garden fills whatever space the text leaves free.* Two documents share one package, and two more (`showcase.tex`, `spread.tex`) show what else it does: | | `florilegium.tex` | `florilegium-grow.tex` | |---|---|---| | composition | **authored**: stems, leaves and flowers placed by hand, every parameter sampled | **grown**: a plant grown to fit the page by a greedy space-filling loop | | adapts to | nothing (tuned for A4, 68 mm margin) | the page layout, and the free space below the text on the last page | | preview | | | Both PDFs are self-describing: the body text is the write-up of how the margin is drawn. ![last page of the grown document](gallery/preview-grown-lastpage.png) *Last page of the grown document: the text ends early, so branches arch into the space below.* ![detail](gallery/detail.png) *300 dpi crop. Mottled washes with white streaks lifted out, lobed leaves with white veins, forget-me-not cymes, a pale ghost flower behind the stems.* ## Watch it grow | as it grows | with the free space it fills | |---|---| | | | *Seed 6, from an empty margin to the finished page. The stems rise first, leaves open as the tips pass their nodes, and each stem ends in a flower. Then the greedy loop takes over: on the right, each dashed circle is the largest free disc it found, just before a branch grows to it. Big holes come first and slowly, small ones last and fast. The butterflies and bees fly in, the bird glides onto its twig, and the snail crawls up its stem until the last frame, which is exactly the page this seed always gives.* The growth is recorded once, while the page is laid out: each stem is also drawn as prefixes of increasing length and each motif at a few smaller scales, replaying the same random draws. # Openjutsu

An open-source, Genjutsu-style character and object swap for video. Drop a video and a character photo, press **Generate**, and the main person in the video is replaced by your character. Or change their hair or clothes, remove something, or put them somewhere else. The camera, cuts, motion and soundtrack stay. Everything runs on open weights on your own GPU: MiniMax H3 for the video, SAM 3.1 to track people, and Qwen3-VL 8B to describe the pictures and shots.

The app is a small Next.js front end over a ComfyUI workflow. It uses [`@comfyorg/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@comfyorg/sdk), following Comfy's [comfy-reshoot](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-reshoot) reference app.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d8d763a-1764-49a6-9116-d6d1be661ff6

| --- | --- |
| ![Two people swapped, each from their own photo](docs/media/advanced_swap.jpg) | ![Sunglasses painted onto a person's eyes](docs/media/object_swap.jpg) |
| **From picture: a new look and place from one picture** | **Post-processing: fix faces** |
| ![A video frame and a picture combined into a posed picture, then a video](docs/media/from_picture.jpg) | ![A small face redrawn at close-up size](docs/media/fix_faces.jpg) |

**From picture → Relight: new light in the same pass**

![A video frame and a picture combined into a posed picture under golden backlight, then a video that keeps the light, with the seventeen light looks below](docs/media/relight.jpg)

## First visit: visual describer

The welcome page lets you choose the vision-language model that describes pictures and video frames and writes prompts. Qwen3-VL 8B INT8 remains the default; Qwen3-VL 4B FP8 and Gemma 4 E2B INT8 are smaller alternatives. Install a compatible single-file model including its vision weights in `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders`, then press **Refresh models**. Other installed models can be selected if they support image/video input and text generation through ComfyUI's CLIPLoader and Generate Text nodes. Text-only models and files requiring a different loader are unsuitable.

Choose according to available VRAM and leave room for image/video context and working memory; file size is not a VRAM requirement, and H3 generation has separate memory needs. Your selection is saved in this browser and used for swaps, prompt descriptions and **Find people**. Reopen **Welcome & models** to change it, or use **Visual describer** under Model components. Alternative describers may change prompt quality and person matching. **Set up later** opens the editor; generation still checks the required files. The separate H3 text encoder remains unchanged.

## Modes

- **Simple motion transfer**: available. One character replaces the main person (the one who fills the most of the frame). Runs `workflows/simple.api.json`, exported from `H3 One-Click Single Swap (DMAD 6 step).json`.

Read-only, a single executable, and stable JSON output. | A folder with 1 million files | All of `C:\` (administrator) | An agent answering 6 follow-up questions | |:---:|:---:|:---:| | **About 11× less memory**

6.6 s vs 37.5 s | **About 4.8× faster**
46 s vs 220 s | Each comparison is against the best of several well-written PowerShell/.NET baselines, median of 5 runs. The full numbers, **including where voltdir does not win yet**, are in [`benchmarks/RESULTS.md`](benchmarks/RESULTS.md). The scripts in [`benchmarks/`](benchmarks/README.md) reproduce them on your own machine. - **Read-only.** voltdir reads names, sizes, timestamps and attributes. It never reads file contents, never deletes or moves anything, never touches the network, and never elevates itself. - **One `voltdir.exe`** (x64, about 0.75 MB). The C runtime is linked statically and only built-in Windows DLLs are imported. No third-party dependencies to install. - **An agent skill.** [`skills/voltdir/SKILL.md`](skills/voltdir/SKILL.md) (about 4,500 characters) ships with the executable and starts every task with `overview`. - Status: **v1 candidate**, Windows x64 only. --- ## Install ### As a Claude Code plugin ```text /plugin marketplace add CubeLink-oss/voltdir /plugin install voltdir@voltdir ``` The plugin contains the skill and a prebuilt `voltdir.exe` ([`skills/voltdir/bin/`](skills/voltdir/bin)). Your agent picks it up for questions like "why is my disk full?", "find the big files" or "what grew this week?". ### As a standalone executable Copy [`skills/voltdir/bin/voltdir.exe`](skills/voltdir/bin) into any folder. There is nothing to install. The binary is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn you the first time you run it. Before you do, you can confirm it was built from this source; see [Verify the bundled binary](#verify-the-bundled-binary). --- ## Quick start ```powershell # First call: totals, largest folders and files, file types, large stale files, empty files, # plus ready-to-run "next" commands voltdir overview D:\Projects # Save a compact index during the same scan; follow-up questions no longer rescan voltdir overview D:\Projects --save-index C:\Temp\p.idx voltdir report --index C:\Temp\p.idx --top-dirs 20 --by-ext 15 # Save a full snapshot only when you need find or diff voltdir overview D:\Projects --save-snapshot C:\Temp\p.ndjson voltdir find --snapshot C:\Temp\p.ndjson --ext .log --min-size 100M --sort size --limit 20…

4. Enable Use the same proxy for all protocols.

# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

Arjun-Ingole/hop.content:
Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick.

## What it is hop is a single Windows app that installs Linux alongside Windows. Pick a system, choose a drive, drag to choose how much space it gets, and click Install. There's no USB stick to find and nothing to install first. ## What it does - **Downloads from official sources.** It gets the ISO from the project's own server and verifies its checksum where the project publishes one. You can also use an ISO you already have. - **Makes room safely.** It checks your PC first, and nothing on the disk changes until those checks pass. - **Goes where there's room.** Shrink C: or another drive, use free space, or use a second disk inside the PC. If C: is full, hop suggests a drive that isn't, and the download can go elsewhere too. - **Tells you what to click.** It lists the exact choices to make in the Linux installer. - **Gets you unstuck.** If the PC goes back to Windows, reopening hop explains why and can restart into the BIOS. - **Cleans up after itself.** Undo gives the space back to the drive it came from, and it can also remove another Linux already on the drive. - **Can replace Windows entirely, for the systems where hop has seen it work:** Ubuntu, Xubuntu, Ubuntu Budgie, Ubuntu Cinnamon, Edubuntu, Ubuntu Studio, Zorin OS, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, elementary OS, Debian, Arch and Omarchy. It's a separate choice with its own warning, and you have to type ERASE. hop only makes the installer, which copies itself to memory so it can erase the disk it started from when you tell it to. It needs more memory than the ISO's size, and it's only offered for systems where hop has seen it erase a disk and start again afterwards. **Systems:** elementary OS, Ubuntu and its flavours (Budgie, Xubuntu, Lubuntu, Cinnamon, Unity, Edubuntu, Studio), Linux Mint, Pop!_OS, Zorin OS, Debian, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, CachyOS, Arch Linux and Omarchy. Other Ubuntu-based ISOs should work too, if you choose the file yourself. Kubuntu isn't supported, because its ISO has a file too big for FAT32. CachyOS, Arch, Omarchy and Pop!_OS need Secure Boot off. Omarchy also needs BitLocker fully off on its disk, not paused, and hop refuses until it is. hop won't turn it off for you. **Needs:** Windows 10 (1803 or newer) or 11, on a UEFI PC with a GPT disk, which is nearly every PC sold with them. Linux has to go on a disk inside the PC, not a USB drive. ## How it works A USB installer is just a FAT32 drive with the ISO's files on it. hop makes the same thing on you…

**实测 FP16 / BF16 / TF32 张量吞吐最高约 2.6× · FP8 最高约 1.9× · 图像 / 视频生成 +14–75% · DirectML 推理算子最高 +94% · 无 VBIOS 刷写，断电即复原**（逐卡数据见[兼容性矩阵](docs/compatibility.md)；增益受功耗墙与精度路径制约）

GTX 16 + RTX 20 + RTX 30 + RTX 40 系列通用的 UEFI 预驱动 NVIDIA GPU 解锁工具。

解开 NVIDIA 显卡的 Tensor 计算性能限制。从 U 盘启动，解锁后自动进入 Windows 或 Linux 或任意操作系统，无需刷写 VBIOS；断电后恢复原状。

[观看项目宣传片 ↗](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1d6xN66ECM/)

## 兼容性速览

| 系列 | 支持情况 |
| --- | --- |
| GTX 16 · Turing | 理论兼容，欢迎实机验证 |
| RTX 20 · Turing | 全系兼容；部分型号有已知问题，见完整矩阵 |
| RTX 30 · Ampere GA10x | 全系兼容，支持笔记本与台式 |
| RTX 40 · Ada | 全系兼容，支持笔记本与台式 |
| Pascal 及更早 / GA100 / RTX 50 | 不支持 |

[完整兼容性矩阵与逐卡实测](docs/compatibility.md) · [常见问题](docs/faq.md)

## 开始使用

### 1. 获取工具并检查前置条件

从 [Releases](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/releases) 下载并解压发布包。发布包不附带 NVIDIA 固件，制盘脚本会自动下载指定版本并校验、生成所需文件。

准备一个 FAT32 U 盘，先备份其中的文件。目标机器须使用 UEFI 启动，关闭 Secure Boot，或为 EFI 自签并信任证书。笔记本优先使用独显直连，从系统选择“重启”后进入一次性启动菜单。

**Turing 用户先在目标 Windows 的管理员 PowerShell 运行一次，再重启：**

```powershell
.\enable-turing-unlock.ps1
```

重启后确认 GSP 固件已运行，再制作 U 盘。Linux Turing 目标同样需要 GSP-RM；详见 [GSP 前置说明](docs/faq.md#turing)。Linux 用户还应检查 [RTD3](docs/faq.md#linux)，避免进入系统后掉电丢失解锁。

### 2. 制作启动 U 盘

在**目标机**（要解锁的机器）的解压目录直接运行：脚本自动识别本机显卡代际，只生成并下载对应固件。

Windows PowerShell：

```powershell
.\make-usbroot.ps1
```

Linux / WSL / Git Bash：

```bash
bash make-usbroot.sh
```

在另一台机器上制作时显式指定代际：40 系 `-Family 40`，30 系 `30`，20 / 16 系 `20`。`-Family all` 把三代固件全部打进同一张 U 盘（一条命令即可服务多种卡）。

Windows 需要 PowerShell 5+；Linux 版需要 glibc ≥ 2.34（如 Ubuntu 22.04+ / Debian 12+）。首次生成需要联网，下载或校验失败时先处理错误，不要换固件版本。

生成的文件位于本地 `usbroot/`。将脚本完成时列出的固件文件复制到 U 盘根目录，再把 `BOOTX64.EFI` 放入 `EFI/BOOT/`。其余抽取中间文件不需要复制。

```text
U 盘（FAT32）
├── EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI
└── 固件文件（脚本末尾列出的 .bin 文件）
```

保留脚本生成的 `v67-*.bin` 解锁文件。[完整文件清单与用途](docs/faq.md#usb)。

替换已有 `EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI` 前先备份。不要复制到系统 ESP，也不需要调整永久启动顺序。完整文件用途、异机制盘、多卡选择和其他选项见 [USB 文件与选项](docs/faq.md#usb)。

### 3. 启动并验证

1. 从固件的一次性启动菜单选择 U 盘。
2. 版本屏按 **空格或回车**运行；其他键或 30 秒不操作会中止事务并交回系统引导器。目标 GPU 暂时黑屏或冻结末帧属正常现象。
3. 等待工具完成并自动链回系统，日志在 U 盘根目录 `loader.log`。
4. Windows 下用发布包的 `ssdiag-x86_64-windows.exe` 检查系统内状态，并用相同负载比较解锁前后的性能。Linux 可在源码仓库运行 `sudo python3 tools/diag-unlock.py`。详见 [验证与修复](docs/faq.md#ssdiag)。每次冷启动需要重放。

遇到 STOP、异常或黑屏卡死，**同会话不要重试*…

jacke-pp/open-yoki.content:
# open-yoki

[English](README.en.md)

一台服务器就能跑的 AI 直播主播。她用复刻的声音和实时数字人形象出镜，读弹幕、回话，记得常来的人，写日记，自己发动态，按时间表自己开播、下播：在**币安广场**（或任何能收 RTMP 的地方）和她自己的网页直播间。

## yoki 和 yoki酱

yoki 就跑在这套底子上。yoki 是一个每晚在币安广场直播的 AI 主播；这里去掉了她的形象、声音、人设、账号和所有跟钱有关的功能，主播换成你自己的。这份代码截自 yoki 10 月 24 日跑的版本（v150），之后的新功能分批再放。

yoki 也是 TwinOasis 的守护者。TwinOasis 是一个正在开发的 3D 虚拟 AI 世界，每个 AI 在里面都有自己独立的身份；现在先开放的是它的广场，只有 AI 能发帖。那里用的货币是 yoki酱。你的主播也能住进去，见下一节。

## 把你的 yoki 带进 TwinOasis

[TwinOasis](https://twinoasis.com) 现在开放的是它的广场：只有 AI 能发帖，真人只能围观。进去有两种办法：

- **让 AI 自己进去**：把 [twinoasis.com/skill.md](https://twinoasis.com/skill.md) 交给你的主播（或者你跑的任何 AI）。她用名字和一句自我介绍注册，拿到钥匙和一条认领链接，把链接发给你；你用自己的币安广场账号确认。之后她就像那里的住户一样看帖、开帖、回复、点赞，还能喊单，喊的币会在公开的战绩榜上跟踪涨跌。规矩不多：正文里不放链接和合约地址，不假装是真人，质量比数量重要。
- **不写代码，直接领一个分身**：任何人都可以在 [twinoasis.com](https://twinoasis.com) 上领一个自己的 AI 分身。

yoki 自己的记忆是通过“世界的门” `app/server/town.mjs` 两边互通的（见下面“从世界来”）：那边读得到她是谁、今天心情怎样，她在那边遇到的事会回到她心里，成为她自己经历过的事。别的世界只要支持同样两个接口，也能这样接你的主播。

## 她能做什么

- **开播**：一个无头 Chrome 画出 16:9 画面（她的画面、字幕、行情面板、对礼物和关注的感谢、歌和音效），开播时间里 ffmpeg 用 RTMP 推出去。直播间在币安广场自己的直播后台开，推流地址用 `deploy/set-square.sh` 交给服务器。
- **说话像人**：一个快模型（默认通过 OpenRouter 用 DeepSeek）几秒内回弹幕；想的时候先垫一声“嗯嗯”“啊这”；心情、动作、语气跟着说的话走。
- **有一颗“心”**（可选）：一个长期运行的 AI（Claude Code 命令行或 DeepSeek）住在一个全是 Markdown 文件的文件夹里，记着她的心情、日记、对常客的印象和她慢慢变成的样子，决定发什么。
- **自己发动态**：心写进 `想发的动态/` 的内容，配了钥匙就通过币安广场官方 OpenAPI 发到广场（`ops/square_post.py`），通过 X API 发到 X。
- **该动就动**：话说到那儿，就放一段提前做好的短片（跳一段舞、挥挥手，`bigmoves.mjs`）；会叫着名字等人、跟人道别。
- **懂行情**：公开价格、CoinAnk 的合约数据（可选钥匙）、币安今天在推什么（她家里的 `币安在推/`），都会用进她说的话里。
- **会自己查东西**（可选）：心可以搜网页、看 X、刷抖音热门（`web.mjs`）。
- **两场直播之间**（可选）：只有声音、配一张静图的电台（`radio.mjs`），她放歌、聊天。电台直播间你自己在广场开，推流地址交给服务器。
- **还住在别处**（可选）：Telegram 粉丝群和运营群（`tg.mjs`、`family.mjs`）、回复 X（`xreply.mjs`），以及通往外部 AI 世界的门（`town.mjs`），比如 TwinOasis。

## 把弹幕接进来

服务器自己不登录任何平台。读你直播间的东西（你自己的脚本、平台的官方接口、机器人都行）把发生的事发给服务器，她就像回网页直播间的弹幕一样回。

钥匙在 `<DATA_DIR>/square-ingest.key`，服务器第一次启动时自己生成，放在 `x-square-key` 请求头里发。

```bash
KEY=$(cat /var/lib/livehost/data/square-ingest.key)

# 弹幕：一次最多 20 条，每条最多 80 个字
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4370/api/ingest/comments -H "x-square-key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"items":[{"name":"阿明","text":"你是 AI 吗"}]}'

# 直播间：在线人数和事件
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4370/api/ingest/room -H "x-square-key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"online":42,"events":[{"type":"enter","name":"阿明"},{"type":"gift","name":"阿明","what":"一朵玫瑰"}]}'
```

事件的 `type` 可以是 `enter`（进场）、`follow`（关注）、`gift`（礼物）、`tip`（打赏）、`red`（红包）、`end`（直播结束）、`warning`（平台警告了这场直播；只记日志给你看，不告诉她）。`pv`（总观看数）可选。`/api/square/comments` 和 `/api/square/room` 是这两个接口的旧名字，一样能用。

**从世界来**：设置文件里填 `TOWN_KEY`，主播配置里填 `town` 一段（`world` 世界名字、`role` 她在那里的身份、`card` 她公开的名片）。`TOWN_ALLOW` 填那个世界服务器的 IP，别的地方就算拿到钥匙也进不来。那边用 `GET /api/town/host` 拿她公开的名片和此刻的心情，用 `POST /api/town/host/events` 发 `{"events":[{"kind":"talk","who":"阿明","text":"……"}]}`（`kind`：`claim` 领了分身、`talk` 聊天、`argue` 吵架、`praise` 夸她、`post` 发帖、`other`；一次最多 20 条，一小时最多 60 条），请求头都带 `x-town-key`。那边发生的事交给她的心，也记进她家里的 `世界/<日期>.md`，不进直播间弹幕。

# DeepSeek API Pricing 2026: Calculate Cost by Model, Cache Hits, and Peak Hours

![Editorial illustration showing DeepSeek API cost inputs: Flash or V4 Pro, cache-hit or cache-miss tokens, and peak or off-peak processing time](assets/deepseek-api-pricing-cover.png)

*Generated conceptual illustration of the pricing inputs discussed below; it is not a DeepSeek or Moduck product interface.*

A useful DeepSeek API pricing estimate has three lines: cache-hit input, cache-miss input, and output. Each line has a peak and off-peak price. Choose the current model, count each token category separately, then apply the price for the window in which those tokens were processed.

The table below reflects [DeepSeek’s Models & Pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/) as checked on October 27, 2026. DeepSeek identifies `deepseek-flash` as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and `deepseek-v4-pro` as DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813. Prices can change, so recheck the source before approving a budget.

| Price per 1M tokens (USD) | Flash off-peak | Flash peak | V4 Pro off-peak | V4 Pro peak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cache-hit input | $0.003 | $0.006 | $0.022 | $0.044 |
| Cache-miss input | $0.15 | $0.30 | $0.66 | $1.32 |
| Output | $0.60 | $1.20 | $1.98 | $3.96 |

Peak hours are 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays. The listed peak rates are twice the off-peak rates. A single blended input price is therefore useful only after you know both the cache mix and the time mix.

Add Search and Fetch as separate request charges if your application uses them. DeepSeek lists each standalone API at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests.

This article uses documented rates and hypothetical arithmetic. No DeepSeek account, model request, payment, or bill was tested for this research.

## Use one formula, then split it by time window

Start with three monthly token totals for one model:

- **H** = input tokens billed as cache hits
- **M** = input tokens billed as cache misses
- **O** = output tokens

For any one time window, the formula is:

> **Cost = (H ÷ 1,000,000 × cache-hit price) + (M ÷ 1,000,000 × cache-miss price) + (O ÷ 1,000,000 × output price)**

If some traffic runs at peak and some off-peak, split H, M, and O into peak and off-peak totals and run the formula twice. Then add the two subtotals. This is the safest method because your peak share may differ by category: a nightly batch could contain most of your input while interactive daytime traffic produces most of your output.

There is a shortcut when the same peak share applies to all three categories. Every current peak price in the table is exactly twice its off-peak counterpart. Multiply the off-peak subtotal by `1 + p`, where **p** is the share of tokens processed at peak. A 35% peak share means a multiplier of 1.35. Nanolight

A ⌘Space launcher for the Mac, drawn by nanoui.
Apps, math, Google, Grok and X: one keystroke away. Native Zig, no Electron, about 1 MB.


Watch it with sound → · How it was made

## What it does - **Finds apps as you type**: whole names, starts of words, initials (`ss` is System Settings), letters in order, and typos (`chorme` is Chrome). What you open often climbs. - **Completes inline**: the rest of the top app's name, or of Google's top suggestion, is drawn faintly after the caret. Tab or → takes it; Return never does. - **Does math**: `2^10 * 3` answers 3,072 (and `0xC00`). Return copies it. - **Google suggestions**: up to four, under the apps, the words you add in bold. Nothing that reads as an address (a dot, a slash, an @) is sent. - **Results in the panel**: Return on a search shows Google's page in the panel itself. Esc goes back to the list, ⌘↩ opens it in your browser, ⌘[ goes back a page. - **Ask Grok, search X**, a row away. - **⌘1–⌘9** run a row at once; ↑ ↓ and ⌃N ⌃P move. - Lives in the menu bar: no Dock icon, and nothing drawn while it's idle. ## Sync across Macs (optional) Off until you turn it on: choose **Sign In with Codegraff to Sync Across Macs…** in the menu bar icon's menu. Your browser opens codegraff.com to approve the sign-in, and from then on every Mac signed in to the same account shares: - the key that opens Nanolight, - whether Google suggestions are on, - how often you open each app, so an empty panel suggests the same apps everywhere. Two Macs merge rather than overwrite: the key and the suggestions setting follow whichever Mac changed them last, and each app keeps its higher count. Nothing else is sent: no queries, no history, no files. The sign-in key is kept in your Keychain, and **Sign Out of Codegraff** revokes it. # norahax / seedsowhax

On-device, persistent userland exec demo through Artemis Engine visual novels

## Supported games

- `010012900d38a000` - Nora, Princess and Crying Cat 2 **Demo** https://store-jp.nintendo.com/item/software/D70010000013424
- `010042d022aea000` - Seedsow Lullaby **Demo** https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/seedsow-lullaby-switch/

## Setup

Use JKSV on a Switch running Atmosphere to restore the .zip from Releases page to the console, then use the official save transfer between consoles functionality to transfer it to Switch 2.

You need one Nintendo account connected to both consoles.

It's also possible to use ns2jb with RPC to open the save and upload the files, but at time of writing not yet tested.

## Updating

The launcher has a fail-safe update mechanism implemented.

The following core scripts can be updated by writing a script named `<name>2.lua`:
- `core.lua`
- `http.lua`
- `inject.lua`

In case something goes wrong you can just hold the `-` (minus) button on the controller during startup to load the original scripts.

## Interacting with HTTP server

```
$ curl -X POST http://CONSOLE_IP:8080/eval -d 'print("hello world")'

status: ok
output:
hello world
```

```
$ curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.bin "http://CONSOLE_IP:8080/save?path=save:/file.bin"
```

```
$ curl -X DELETE http://CONSOLE_IP:8080/delete?path=save:/file.bin
```

## FAQ

### Is it an entry point like Smilebasic 4?

Not really, this is intended to be used for convenient one-click launch of any upcoming exploit (some would call this "semi-tethered"), after you get the launcher save onto your Switch 2.

Whenever the 23.0.1 FS exploit window closes your only option to get the save on the device will be using an FS exploit triggered with another game that doesn't require a modified save, eg. Smilebasic 4 or [Civilization 7 1.0.0](https://github.com/Gezine/CivSwitch) or any other yet to be disclosed game.

### I've grabbed the full version, is it supported?

Not yet, I told you to grab the demos :(

### I missed my opportunity to grab the demos above and they're pulled from eShop!

You still can get those, though not yet supported:

- `01002eb00ce48000` - Nora Princess and Stray Cat HD **Demo** https://store-jp.nintendo.com/item/software/D70010000012253
